analysis: Only documentation and changelog changed: the new changelog.d/switch-model-cache-directory.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 296-297. They state that `darkbloom switch` now scans local models in the `model_cache_directory` from the daemon's resolved provider.toml. The code change itself is not in the supplied evidence. I found no new endpoints, credentials, authorization changes or attestation changes in the supplied text. The relevant assets and threats are A-004 and T-012, plus the model-weight substitution threat T-027. The doc still says the provider validates artifacts and hashes before the switch, and that the coordinator validates the selection (cli-reference.md lines 298-330). The documented trust assumption is unchanged: operator-controlled cache directories were already within the threat model, and the weight-hash checks apply to whichever directory the daemon uses. The next pass should check the code that implements this, if it ships in another batch. That check is whether the picker and `--all` scan reads the same effective model_cache_directory as the daemon. It should also confirm that hash validation and model-ID or path handling still run on a custom directory, with no symlink or path traversal. I cannot confirm this from the docs alone. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression.
